Perhaps this is a comment for another subverse, but I think Voat would need other strategies to gain traction. Maybe they are working on it already, but I imagine an embedded comment section for bloggers, journals, etc would help. It might require an open ID. Users would simply enter a comment at the referred site and it would be appended here, or open a new post. Being this a faster way to post, it would reduce reposting, since the bridge could be unique. Also, it would allow to establish a policy for multiverse posting.

Both parties would benefit of the increase in traffic. Libertarian blogs and mags should be especially willing to cooperate, given the freedom vibe in Voat...

Alternatively, they could develop a Voat browser extension that shows the comments related to the webpage you are visiting and even suggests alternative posts referring to other pages with the same information/topic. This would be a great way to redirect traffic from pages that have not been posted here to those that have.

The embedded comments option would bring both users and content, but would depend on the cooperation of webmasters. The browser extension would not bring new users directly, but would greatly increase the content.

I understand reddit's business model might want the users navigating within their site and stumbling upon (pun intended) their ads, but Voat doesn't rely on ads and this would be a strategy to benefit from that difference. It might also help reduce the traffic load and favor a P2P approach.

Charly Keunang shot and killed by LAPD. Police were investigating possible involvement in a crime, claim Keunang resisted commands and wanted to fight, resisted taser, reached for gun. March 1, 2015

Small summary of the article

Los Angeles Police officers approached Keunang around noon after receiving a 911 call reporting that he had been involved in some kind of robbery or assault, Police Chief Charlie Beck told reporters.

Keunang allegedly refused to follow the officers’ commands, and instead, tried to fight them, investigators say. The officers used a Taser to try to subdue him, but Keunang continued to resist and fell to the ground, according to an LAPD news release.

During the struggle, investigators say Keunang grabbed a rookie officer’s holstered pistol, prompting three other officers to open fire.

Beck told reporters there are videos from nearby security cameras and two of the officers' body cameras that are also being reviewed.

Keunang's family filed a $20-million claim against the city on April 30, saying the police “initiated” a struggle that ended in a “cop-created killing.”
